summary: This is a Mol Labs public report (L22) proposing a C. elegans experimental design to test whether metformin retains lifespan/healthspan benefits independently of AMPK signaling. The document frames an "assumption-kill" hypothesis: if AMPK genetic loss-of-function (aak-2 alleles) or Compound C abolishes AMPK-class lifespan/healthspan attribution, does metformin still retain ≥50% of its median lifespan improvement relative to AMPK-intact controls? The experiment has NOT been run; the document synthesizes prior art (Onken 2010, Martin-Montalvo 2013, Foretz 2010, Kalender 2010) and defines prediction variables, refutation criteria, and actionable limitations.

content_blocks.title: Document Overview and Hypothesis (L22)
content_blocks.content: Mol Labs public report L22 proposes a pre-registered C. elegans panel experiment to test whether metformin retains lifespan/healthspan benefits when AMPK signaling is abolished. The core claim: under AMPK/aak-2 genetic LOF or Compound C match that abolishes AMPK-class lifespan/healthspan attribution, metformin vs vehicle median lifespan improvement retains ≥50% of the improvement seen on AMPK-intact concurrent controls. Execution status: NOT_RUN. This is a research discussion / propose-assay document, not a completed experiment.

content_blocks.title: Claim / Experimental Design
content_blocks.content: Pre-registered C. elegans panel: metformin vs vehicle under AMPK/aak-2 genetic LOF (or Compound C match abolishing AMPK-class control) vs AMPK-intact concurrent controls. Primary referee: median lifespan (days). Optional co-readouts: healthspan, locomotion, lipofuscin (secondary only, not gate). Threshold: block-arm median lifespan improvement (metformin vs vehicle under block) retains ≥50% of metformin vs vehicle median lifespan improvement on AMPK-intact concurrent controls. α/N pre-specified. Refutation criterion: <50% retention when block-not-abolished, underpowered-strata, and assay-mismatch artifacts are ruled out.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art Summary
content_blocks.content:
Four key prior art references are cited:
1. Onken/Driscoll (PMID 20090912, PLoS One 2010): Metformin extends C. elegans healthspan; AMPK/AAK-2 and LKB1/PAR-4 are essential — aak-2 alleles (ok524, rr48): no tested metformin concentration extends lifespan; metformin is detrimental without AMPK/LKB1. This establishes NECESSITY (inverse of residual) against residual lifespan/healthspan claim.
2. Martin-Montalvo (PMID 23900241, Nat Commun 2013): 0.1% dietary metformin extends male mouse healthspan and lifespan; increases AMPK activity. Phenotype prior; no AMPK genetic LOF or Compound C residual lifespan H2H on same panel.
3. Foretz (PMID 20577053, JCI 2010): Metformin inhibits hepatic gluconeogenesis independently of LKB1/AMPK via hepatic energy state. AMPK-independent metabolic arm; ≠ residual lifespan under AMPK abolish.
4. Kalender (PMID 20444419, Cell Metab 2010): Metformin inhibits mTORC1 independent of AMPK via Rag GTPases. AMPK-independent mTORC1 arm; ≠ residual lifespan under AMPK abolish.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: AMPK-insufficiency assumption-kill: Onken/Driscoll PLoS One shows AMPK/AAK-2 and LKB1/PAR-4 essential for metformin C. elegans healthspan (necessity, inverse of residual). aak-2 alleles — no tested metformin concentration extends lifespan; metformin detrimental without AMPK/LKB1. Martin-Montalvo grounds mouse lifespan/healthspan phenotype without AMPK-abolish residual arm. Foretz hepatic gluconeogenesis and Kalender Rag-mTORC1 are AMPK-independent metabolic arms — adjacent NON-MATCH for residual lifespan H2H. Preferred model: C. elegans lifespan proxy ± metformin ± aak-2/AMPK LOF (or Compound C match) before new rodent or human dosing. Mouse residual under systemic AMPK LOF only optional long arm.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations and Competing Caveats
content_blocks.content:
1. L1–L21 do not prove L22 — new parent area metformin-ampk-insufficiency; Onken/Martin-Montalvo/Foretz/Kalender are necessity or metabolic adjacent, not residual-positive H2H under AMPK abolish; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated prediction-failure; do not invent residual.
2. PMID 20090912 NECESSITY constrains residual C. elegans healthspan/lifespan; PMID 20577053/20444419 wrong endpoints for residual lifespan; PMID 23900241 lacks AMPK-abolish residual arm — matched residual-positive lifespan/healthspan H2H UNKNOWN — PRIOR_ART PARTIAL.
3. Competing caveats: block not actually abolishing AMPK-class control benefit / underpowered strata / referee-assay mismatch leave the test inconclusive rather than refuted.
4. L15 (DunedinPACE/GrimAge), L16 (tissue SA-β-gal/p16 vs blood under D+Q), L17 (intermittent-rapa FKBP), L18 (17α-E2 caloric-match), L19 (acarbose glycemic-match), L20 (SPD/ATG bulk autophagy; AMPK ≠ bulk ATG), L21 (UA/mitophagy; AMPK ≠ mitophagy) are all explicitly NOT equivalent to L22. NOT NAD-after-senolysis.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis
content_blocks.content:
Three critical ablations identified:
1. Removing matched metformin ± aak-2/AMPK LOF (or Compound C match) vs AMPK-intact concurrent controls with same-panel median lifespan residual co-readout: Without the block-lock × residual lifespan H2H on the same panel, separate Onken necessity LITERATURE and Foretz/Kalender metabolic adjacent cannot show lifespan ≠ mere AMPK-sole-necessity bridge, and residual-positive stays untested.
2. Removing block-arm median lifespan improvement scored against the AMPK-intact metformin vs vehicle median lifespan improvement as named comparator: Without the intact-arm comparator under the block lock, the card collapses into unmatched necessity framing and loses the ampk-insufficiency assumption-kill.
3. Removing L15≠L22 through L21≠L22 discipline and residual-UNKNOWN constraints: Treating adjacent experiments or empty PubMed as deciding residual-positive under AMPK abolish — or inventing residual effect sizes — would invent a result left UNKNOWN.

key_findings: Experiment NOT_RUN — this is a proposed assay design, not a completed experiment; TRL is effectively TRL 1 (concept/hypothesis stage).

Onken/Driscoll (PMID 20090912) establishes NECESSITY: AMPK/AAK-2 and LKB1/PAR-4 are essential for metformin C. elegans healthspan/lifespan; aak-2 alleles abolish lifespan extension; metformin is detrimental without AMPK/LKB1.

Martin-Montalvo (PMID 23900241) shows 0.1% dietary metformin extends male mouse healthspan and lifespan and increases AMPK activity, but lacks an AMPK genetic LOF or Compound C residual lifespan H2H arm.

Foretz (PMID 20577053) and Kalender (PMID 20444419) demonstrate AMPK-independent metabolic mechanisms (hepatic gluconeogenesis via energy state; mTORC1 via Rag GTPases) but these are explicitly classified as NON-MATCH for residual lifespan under AMPK abolish.
Residual-positive metformin lifespan or healthspan H2H under AMPK genetic LOF or Compound C match that abolishes AMPK-class control is classified as UNKNOWN — no such data exists in the literature.

Prediction threshold: block-arm median lifespan improvement (metformin vs vehicle under AMPK block) must retain ≥50% of AMPK-intact metformin vs vehicle median lifespan improvement to support the assumption-kill hypothesis.

Refutation criterion: <50% retention (when block-not-abolished, underpowered-strata, and assay-mismatch artifacts are ruled out) would confirm metformin lifespan reduces to mere AMPK-necessary bridge.
Estimated time to refute: 4 weeks; kill_cost_tier=1; ip_class=ampk-insufficiency; vault_hold=no.
Prior art is classified as PARTIAL: necessity is established against residual, but matched residual-positive lifespan/healthspan H2H remains absent from the literature.
L15 through L21 (other Mol Labs hypotheses) are explicitly not equivalent to L22 and do not constitute proof of residual AMPK-independent metformin lifespan benefit.
